contents.entry: Pointers: parent, siblings, DAG and principles
Shared needs: what the shared author declares for this node
Input record: unit.start of the two system units
Mechanism: two system units, per-run seat units, one clock, the tick loops, one health answer
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
Retries up to 3, then recover and report
State paths and the cleanup script for each

pointers.sibling: JSON schema of unit.start in and tick, health out
pointers.principle: Rule 2 (no cog: N-06 owns the clock, nothing starts by an agent typing) and rule 7 (herdr is the owner's window; every system process is its own supervised unit)
The collision answer every node gives: leases with fencing tokens, compare-and-swap, idempotent steps, 409 that reports
pointers.needs: The shared anchors this volume relies on, declared as needs until shared/ lands
pointers.shared: The service and launcher users these units run as
Seats run as pool users in their own units
The per-run unit and the run entity the launcher adopts by
Ticks and health write no record unless the state changes
Store or host down is seen from outside the host
N-06 imports the probe journal and replays the emergency journal on recovery
Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

shared-needs.rule: shared/ belongs to the shared author (brief C, "What R-03 produces"); this volume never writes it and never points into it before it exists. Each need names the volume and the anchor the shared author declares. check.sh (N-46) resolves a need by volume and anchor once the shared volume lands, so a need becomes a live pointer without a hand edit. The same needs are returned to the shared author as data by the seat that wrote this volume.
shared-needs.need: Rows for unit.started 100; tick.daily 100; health.recovered 200; reload.applied 200; tick.missed 500; unit.crashloop 500; unit.duplicate 500; reload.failed 500; host.outage 500; health.unhealthy 503. tick and health are entity-only kinds and carry no code row of their own. Owner-acts: unit.crashloop; health.unhealthy with reason store, disk or crashloop; tick.missed at three in an hour; three watchdog restarts in an hour.
Entities tick:<subkind> (n, at, interval_seconds, class for backup), entity-only (shared/contracts.xml#entity-only): written by compare-and-swap once per tick, no record except tick.missed.
Entity health:service (status, reasons[], counters, version, config_hash, at) and table health_history(at, status, reasons JSON) appended on transition; pruned by cleanup-logs.sh --health.
The system comes up before humans and agents; the unit is 100 percent operational and checked before the line is kicked (global rule: design first, system first).
Every wait has a timeout and a fallback; nothing starts by an agent typing; the clock is the only trigger.
The owner's always-on monitor never stops on a halt: ticks, health, backups, the poll and the push transport keep running under hold (memory rule bearings-stable-is-the-only-always-on-monitor).

tick intervals scheduler 5, poll 30, stall 15, health 15, backup 21600, daily 00:05Z; drain_seconds 30, reload_seconds 10, health.check_seconds 2, health.keep_days 30, logs.keep_days 14; env COQ_STATE, COQ_REPO and the secrets file path; a missing key is exit 3 naming the key; exit 4 is a duplicate instance and nothing else.

Restart=always in 5 s, StartLimitIntervalSec=0 (never give up), RestartPreventExitStatus=4; unit.started with reason; three in ten minutes is unit.crashloop and one card; seats are untouched by a service restart.

A second binary started by hand: flock on STATE/run/service.lock (or STATE/run/launcher.lock) refuses, exit 4, unit.duplicate 500 naming the holder pid; RestartPreventExitStatus=4 keeps systemd from looping on it.
WSL suspend and wake: tickers fire once each, the tick counter shows the gap, tick.missed once per subkind.

purpose.is: N-06 is the machine that starts the factory: two systemd system units run the two long-lived processes as their own users (shared/authority.xml#principals): coq-svc.service runs coq-service (every node in-process, the one clock, the store) as coq-svc, and coq-launch.service runs the launcher (N-15) as coq-launch. The clock emits every tick the other nodes run on, and the service answers health for the whole line.

Seats are never children of either unit: each run is its own transient unit coq-seat-<run_id> in coq-launch's user manager (shared/contracts.xml#run-states), so restarting, upgrading or watchdog-killing a service unit kills no seat; the launcher adopts its runs by unit name when it comes back.

It is the root of the DAG's time: no node polls on its own timer and no agent starts anything; the system comes up before humans and agents, like starting the machines before the line is kicked (global rule: design first, system first).
purpose.is-not: It is not herdr: herdr is the owner's window only (D08, C46); no pane hosts this process, and no node calls herdr to schedule, route or store. It is not a container: the small cut runs the binaries on the host under systemd (D22, C38), not in Podman (containers deferred, shared/authority.xml).
purpose.decisions: D01, D08 (C46: every system process is its own supervised unit), D22 (C38), D09 (C41: small cut, keep interfaces and the fake clock), SPEC-16 sh-unit (one supervised unit, domain loops as goroutines) kept.

record.who: The system manager (systemd PID 1), at boot (WantedBy=multi-user.target), on crash through Restart=always, or on `sudo systemctl start coq-svc` by the owner.
record.field: COQ_STATE, COQ_REPO and the secrets file path; nothing else; every tunable is in scheduler/config/scheduler.json (a missing key is exit 3 naming the key).

also.note: reload tables and config; the clock and the ticks are not restarted
read every tick; a hold stops seat grants, work-class leases and merges, never ticks, health, backups or the probe import (a halt never stops monitoring)

record.field: scheduler (tick.scheduler_seconds 5), poll (forge.poll_seconds 30), backup (backup.interval_seconds 21600, with class), stall (stall.tick_seconds 15), daily (tick.daily_at 00:05Z).
A per-subkind counter that only grows since start, with the start id, so a late or doubled tick is detectable.
record.rule: tick is an entity-only kind (shared/contracts.xml#entity-only): the entity tick:SUBKIND is CAS-written every tick and broadcast in-process to the node loops, and no record is appended; the log gets only tick.missed 500 and tick.daily 100. Book 1.0 said the same but every entity write was also a record (NF-A7); the entity-only registration is what makes it true.

record.field: serving or not_serving, the grpc.health.v1 answer, plus the reason list when not serving.
store (N-01), forge (N-04 snapshot age), backup (N-05 age), leases (sweep age), ticks (every subkind's age), disk (free under STATE), unit (pid, started_at, version, config hash).
Every counter the six G1 nodes and the other service nodes expose, by name, reset at start (SPEC-16.I kept as the shape: counters live in the answer, no metrics server).
record.rule: health is an entity-only kind: health:service is CAS-written every health.tick_seconds and pushed by N-31 as an entity frame; the log gets health.unhealthy 503 and health.recovered 200 once per status transition, never per tick.

mechanism.component: Two system unit files, installed by `sudo make -C scheduler install-units` into /etc/systemd/system/ (sources scheduler/host/systemd/coq-svc.service and coq-launch.service, planned): coq-svc.service: User=coq-svc, Group=coq-svc, Type=notify, ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/coq-service run, RuntimeDirectory=coq (mode 0750, so /run/coq holds store.sock and control.sock), Restart=always, RestartSec=5, StartLimitIntervalSec=0, RestartPreventExitStatus=4, WatchdogSec=60, TimeoutStopSec=drain_seconds plus 10, KillMode=mixed, EnvironmentFile=STATE/config/service.env, UMask=0077, NoNewPrivileges=yes. coq-launch.service: User=coq-launch, Group=coq-launch, SupplementaryGroups=coq-store, Type=notify, ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/coq-launcher run, Requires and After coq-svc.service, the same Restart, StartLimit, RestartPreventExitStatus and Watchdog values, KillMode=mixed. Restart and StartLimit agree in both: restart every 5 s forever (a crash loop is visible in health history and through unit.crashloop; giving up is the 9.5 h dark outage of L06 section 5.2), except exit 4, which a restart cannot fix. KillMode=mixed is safe because neither cgroup holds a seat.

The launcher starts each run with `systemd-run --user --unit=coq-seat-<run_id> --collect -p KillMode=control-group -p TimeoutStopSec=<kill.grace_seconds> -p RuntimeMaxSec=<bound>` in coq-launch's own user manager (`loginctl enable-linger coq-launch`, an install step), whose ExecStart is coq-seat-exec start and whose ExecStop is coq-seat-exec kill (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation). The unit is in user@<coq-launch uid>.service, not in coq-svc.service or coq-launch.service, so stopping either service unit leaves it running; on start the launcher lists coq-seat-* units and adopts each by the run entity run:<run_id> (shared/contracts.xml#run-states). Only the kill authority of shared/contracts.xml#kill-authority stops a seat unit.

core.Clock (scheduler/internal/core/interfaces.go) with the real implementation returning time.Now().UTC() and testkit.Clock for tests; every node receives the clock by injection; nothing calls time.Now directly (go vet rule in lint: a grep for time.Now outside clock.go fails the build).

Package scheduler/internal/unit: one goroutine per subkind on a time.Ticker from the clock; each tick writes the entity tick:SUBKIND and sends on a per-subkind channel with a buffer of 1; a slow consumer coalesces ticks (level-triggered consumers do not need every tick, T03), and a consumer that has not drained in two intervals is reported tick.missed with the subkind.

grpc.health.v1.Health on the control socket /run/coq/control.sock (coq-svc:coq-store, mode 0660) plus Status (the SPEC-16 Scheduler service shape: Health, Status, Reload, Drain, Retry kept on the same proto, generated code regenerated by `make proto` in the build container). Every check is a function returning ok or a reason with a bound of health.check_seconds 2; a check over its bound is a reason itself.
mechanism.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant SD as systemd (system manager) participant U as coq-service run participant ST as N-01 store participant T as tick loops participant H as health SD->>U: ExecStart as coq-svc (boot, or Restart) U->>U: resolve STATE (state-root rule), load config (exit 3 on a missing key) U->>ST: open, quick_check, migrate (3 attempts) ST-->>U: SERVING or NOT_SERVING U->>U: recover: N-02 leases, N-03 claims, N-05 temps (its backup:store lease is swept by N-02) U->>ST: replay STATE/run/emergency.jsonl, import the probe journal U->>T: start scheduler, poll, backup, stall, daily loops U->>H: serve control.sock, store.sock U->>SD: READY=1 loop every 20 s T->>SD: WATCHDOG=1 end loop every 15 s H->>ST: CAS health:service, latched transitions to the log end SD->>U: SIGTERM U->>T: stop ticks U->>ST: finish in-flight, checkpoint TRUNCATE, close U->>SD: exit 0 within drain_seconds
mechanism.schedule: Scheduler 5 s, poll 30 s, stall 15 s, health 15 s, backup every 6 h with class tick, daily at 00:05Z (and backup class daily at the first backup tick after 03:00Z, monthly at the first daily of a month). All from config keys named in record.schema.json; a tick interval under 1 s or over a day is a config validation error at start.
mechanism.hold: The entity flag:hold (written only by N-44) is read into memory on every scheduler tick; N-02's grant guard and N-09 check it; ticks, health, backups, the forge poll, the push transport and every maintenance lease keep running under hold, because the owner's monitor never stops on a halt.
mechanism.recovery: On every start and on every transition of the store check to serving, N-06 replays STATE/run/emergency.jsonl (operation key N-06/emergency.replay/<sha256 of the line>/r1) and imports the probe's journal as host.outage records (operation key N-06/host.outage/<outage_id>/r1), per shared/outside-probe.xml#journal; both are replays when repeated.
mechanism.counters: Every node registers counters by name at start; Status returns them all; a reset at start is itself a counter (unit.restarts_total is read from the health history in the store, so it survives restarts).

start.rule: Nothing starts by an agent typing. The system manager starts both units at boot; a crash is restarted in 5 s; a hang is killed by the watchdog and restarted. The owner's only hand action is the one-time install in the runbook.
start.step: Install once, as the owner with sudo: `sudo make -C scheduler install-units` runs scheduler/host/bin/install-users.sh (planned: creates coq-svc, coq-launch, the coq-seat-01..16 pool and group coq-store per shared/authority.xml#principals), copies the binaries to /usr/local/bin, writes both unit files, runs `systemctl daemon-reload`, `enable --now coq-svc coq-launch` and `loginctl enable-linger coq-launch`; the Makefile target is the one hand step and it is a script in the repository.
Start sequence as in the diagram; unit.started 100 with version, config hash, STATE path and reason; READY=1 only after the store is SERVING and the sockets listen.

A start that cannot open the store after 3 attempts still reaches READY=1 with health not_serving and reason store; nothing is carded through the store that cannot open. The stable page's /livez reports store down and the outside probe alerts the owner within its bound (shared/outside-probe.xml#probe, #alerting); records that could not commit go to the emergency journal and are replayed on recovery.

The old bash watchers (route.sh, flow.sh, policy.sh, the five watch scripts) are not started by anything once this unit is enabled; N-49 and N-50 retire their units and cache copies (04-UNLANDED section 8).

wait.name: store-open
wait.fallback: READY with health not_serving; the outside probe alerts (shared/outside-probe.xml#alerting); the unit keeps retrying the open every health tick so a fixed disk recovers without a restart

wait.name: tick-consumer
wait.on: a node loop draining its tick channel
wait.fallback: tick.missed 500 for the subkind; the tick is coalesced, never queued; health lists the slow subkind

wait.name: health-check
wait.fallback: the check reports timeout as its reason; the health answer is never blocked by one check

wait.name: watchdog
wait.fallback: systemd kills and restarts the unit, never a seat (seats are in their own units); unit.started reason watchdog; three watchdog restarts in an hour is an owner-acts code through N-28

wait.name: probe-import
wait.on: the probe's journal over the tailnet
wait.fallback: leave the journal on the Pi and retry on the next daily tick

wait.name: drain
wait.fallback: exit anyway; systemd's TimeoutStopSec kills at drain plus 10; the store's WAL makes that safe

wait.name: reload
wait.fallback: the old tables stay loaded; reload.failed 500 names the key; the ctl call returns the failure

retries.rule: Every automated step retries up to 3 times, then recovers and reports.
retries.step: 3 attempts at start, then not_serving with the open retried every health tick thereafter (recovery without the owner when the cause clears); the owner hears of it from the outside probe, not from a card, and the outage is recorded as host.outage on recovery.

Restart=always with RestartSec 5 and no start limit, except exit 4; each start appends unit.started with reason; three crashes in ten minutes is unit.crashloop 500 and one card; running seats are not touched and are adopted by the launcher. A crash loop that also keeps the store down is seen by the outside probe (L06 section 5.2: the in-host dead man's switch never fired in a 9.5 h outage).
A CAS 409 on health:service (only possible after a restart overlap) is re-read and rewritten once; a store 503 skips this tick's write and the next tick writes.
A failed reload is reported and not retried by itself; the next `ctl reload` or SIGHUP tries again; the running tables are never half-replaced.

many-agents.reading: Every node, screen and seat reads one health entity and the tick entities through the store or N-31; the Status RPC is read-only and serves any number of callers concurrently.
many-agents.working: One process per unit is the rule: each unit's single instance plus a flock (STATE/run/service.lock for coq-service, STATE/run/launcher.lock for the launcher) taken at start; a second binary started by hand exits 4 with unit.duplicate 500 before touching the store, so two clocks can never tick one store; RestartPreventExitStatus=4 keeps a doubled unit from looping.
many-agents.collision: A hand start while the unit runs: the flock refuses; the record names the pid that holds it.

systemd restarts coq-svc while a scheduler tick dispatches: GrantDispatch is one Commit under one operation key (N-07), so the new instance's first tick finds the lease reserved and does not dispatch twice.

The owner upgrades and restarts both units while eight seats run: the seats are in their coq-seat-* units in coq-launch's user manager and keep running; their heartbeats miss at most one interval (lease ttl is far longer, shared/contracts.xml#timing); the new launcher lists the units and adopts each by run:<run_id>; no attempt is charged (F11).

The host sleeps and wakes (WSL suspend): the tickers fire once each, not once per missed interval (Go's Ticker drops ticks), the tick counter shows the gap, and tick.missed is reported once per subkind.

The owner sets hold during a tick: the flag is read at the start of the tick; a dispatch already past the check completes (it holds a lease and will finish); the next tick holds. Hold is a level, not an interrupt.

A dev or uat tier page idle-stops or stops unclean: N-06 counts the page.down (100 for a clean idle stop, 500 for a crash) on that tier's own lamp and in its restart counter; it writes no alert and no wake, and a STOPPED from a non-stable tier is a record, never a prompt to the architect (nodes/N-32/spec.xml#tier-rules, rule wake-only-stable). Only a stable-tier page.down 500 or watcher.dead 500 reaches the owner, as a card through N-28.
A reload swaps tables between ticks under a RWMutex; a tick in progress keeps the old pointer; the next tick sees the new.
many-agents.test: With testkit.Clock: 24 h of simulated ticks in under a second, with a suspend gap of 2 h, three injected crashes and two reloads: every subkind's counter is monotonic, exactly one tick.missed per subkind for the gap, health transitions appear once each in the log, and the lock refuses a second instance.

emits.acts: nobody; N-51 counts restarts in the day's audit
N-51 (exit test), N-05 (daily class), N-45 (timer cleanups)
nobody; N-43 reads the loaded hash
N-06 itself (health reason); owner card at three in an hour
the person who typed the second start; the record says so (exit 4)
the caller; the config ticket is wrong
owner, at most one card per outage_id after the fact; the probe already alerted (shared/outside-probe.xml#journal)
owner through N-28 when the reason is owner-acts (store, disk, crashloop); otherwise the named node's own fallback

status-codes.rule: Every code above must exist in ../../shared/status-codes.xml#codes with the same meaning and actor.

path.cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-unit.sh --apply (owner, sudo): disable --now both units, remove the unit files and the binaries; dry-run prints the commands
scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh removes them when no live pid holds the lock; refuses otherwise
truncated by N-06's replay only after every line committed; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh never touches it
kept on purpose; listed in the README so cleanup-run.sh skips it by name; only the owner removes it, by break glass

path.writer: N-06 structured log (starts, ticks missed, health transitions, reloads)

path.cleanup: systemd removes /run/coq at stop; scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-run.sh removes a stale one
the file is the owner's (N-01 owns it); health_history rows older than health.keep_days 30 are pruned on the daily tick by scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-logs.sh --health through a Commit
journald's own retention; `journalctl --vacuum-time=14d` is in scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-logs.sh --journal

out.record: health record whose status maps to owner-acts
health and hold state for the controls frame
daily tick for the exit test

also.note: in-group consumers; the drawn edges go through N-07 and N-12

item.check: Both unit files have their User, Type=notify, Restart=always, RestartSec=5, StartLimitIntervalSec=0, RestartPreventExitStatus=4, WatchdogSec=60; coq-svc has RuntimeDirectory=coq and EnvironmentFile under STATE.
item.proof: `systemctl cat coq-svc coq-launch` saved in the test log; scheduler/host/tests asserts the keys (not-run).

item.check: A seat started by the launcher is in user@<coq-launch uid>.service/app.slice/coq-seat-<run_id>.service; `systemctl restart coq-svc coq-launch` leaves it running and the launcher adopts it.
item.proof: Host test: start a sleep seat, restart both units, read /proc/PID/cgroup before and after, find run.adopted (not-run).

item.check: READY=1 is sent only after the store is SERVING and both sockets listen.
WATCHDOG=1 is sent every 20 s from the tick loop; a blocked loop stops it.
item.proof: Test with a blocked loop and a captured NOTIFY_SOCKET: no ping after the block.

item.check: Every subkind ticks at its configured interval and the tick entity's version grows by one per tick.
A consumer slower than two intervals yields one tick.missed and coalesced ticks, never a queue.
health:service is written every 15 s and transitions appear once each in the log.
Hold stops dispatch and merges only; ticks, health, backup and poll continue.
item.proof: Integration test with flag:hold set: N-07 dispatch count 0, tick counters growing.

item.check: A second instance exits 4 with unit.duplicate, and systemd does not restart it; a missing config key exits 3.
item.proof: Script test starting the binary twice and once with a key removed (not-run).

item.check: With the store unable to open, no card is attempted; /livez reports store down; after recovery the emergency journal is replayed once and host.outage is imported once per outage.
item.proof: Host test on a test state root (not-run; shared/outside-probe.xml lists the go-live proof).

item.check: SIGTERM drains within drain_seconds and exits 0; the WAL is checkpointed.
item.proof: Script test; wal file size 0 after exit.

item.check: No time.Now outside the clock implementation.
Every state path above has its cleanup script, dry-run by default, registered in N-45.
item.proof: Each script run with no flags prints and exits 0; the registry lists them.

item.check: The units start at boot without a login, and coq-launch's user manager runs without a login.
item.proof: `systemctl is-enabled coq-svc coq-launch` and `loginctl show-user coq-launch -p Linger` say yes; a reboot test shows unit.started reason boot (not-run).

actor.name: systemd (system manager)
actor.may: start, stop, restart, watchdog-kill coq-svc.service and coq-launch.service

actor.name: coq-launch's user manager
actor.may: run and stop the coq-seat-* units; only the launcher asks it to (shared/contracts.xml#kill-authority)

actor.name: N-06 in-process
actor.may: write tick and health entities, the lock and pid, notify systemd

actor.name: N-44 (code)
actor.may: set and clear flag:hold (the only flag writer), from N-29 rulings and N-42 controls

actor.name: N-43 (code)
actor.may: call Reload after a status-code map commit

actor.name: seat (the model)
actor.may: nothing: a pool user cannot reach the control socket or manage either unit (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation)

actor.name: owner
actor.may: install, enable, start, stop, restart with sudo; `scheduler ctl health` and status over the control socket (group coq-store); set hold from the Controls screen; break glass is the only path to stop the units while the line runs, and the stop itself is recorded by the drain

monitoring.surface: The Controls screen (N-42) shows the unit as the reactor: running, hold, build-mode, watcher lamp, health reasons; the Map (N-38) shows the clock as the belt drive; Alerts (N-41) shows health.unhealthy, unit.crashloop, tick.missed. The bearings page (N-32) shows staleness from the health entity's age, so a dead unit is visible as a stale page within one health interval.

runbook.task: `make -C scheduler build` then `sudo make -C scheduler install-units`; `systemctl status coq-svc coq-launch` shows both active (running).
`scheduler ctl health` (the grpc.health.v1 answer plus reasons) and `scheduler ctl status` (counters, ticks, tables, held and dead jobs).
`journalctl -u coq-svc -u coq-launch -f` for the processes; STATE/logs/service/*.jsonl for structured lines by node.
Merge the config ticket; `scheduler ctl reload`; reload.applied names the hashes.
From the Controls screen (N-42) or `scheduler ctl hold set --reason ...` (a control.action through N-29, applied by N-44); clearing it is an owner ruling; ticks and monitoring never stop.

`sudo systemctl restart coq-svc coq-launch`; the drain finishes in-flight Commits; seats keep running in their own units; leases survive (N-02 recover); the launcher adopts its runs; nothing is lost and no attempt is charged.
`make -C scheduler build` then `sudo make -C scheduler install-units`, then restart; the version appears in unit.started.

item.what: every long-running process is a labelled herdr pane; the container runs in one, the executor in one
item.reason: C46 ruled herdr is the owner's window only and every system process is its own supervised unit; RC6 named one herdr server hosting everything as a root cause

item.what: the scheduler in a rootless Podman container with an executor on the host behind a unix socket
item.reason: the small cut (C41) runs one binary on the host under systemd; there is no herdr pane to type into, so the executor verb table has no job; builds and tests still run in Podman (l-make kept), the service does not

item.what: belt.file and belt.stale_seconds as the liveness signal; seat.busy_regex and seat.done_regex screen reads
item.reason: liveness is systemd's watchdog plus the health entity's age; screen regexes are K04 and V08 violations (an LLM screen is not a probe)

item.what: watchdog.timer as a separate dead man's switch unit
item.reason: item 10 is honoured by WatchdogSec in the same unit plus the bearings page staleness; a second unit that counts records was the one that never fired (L06 section 5.2); the exit test (N-51) is the outside-the-line timer that remains

item.what: ~/.cache/coq-watch/patrol-tick.sh and watchdog.sh as running line processes
item.reason: their probes are health checks here; the scripts are retired by N-49 under the LAND verdicts of WO-20261013-9617 and WO-20261013-bf70, which fold into this node

item.what: one systemd user unit as the owner with KillMode=mixed and the seats as child process groups (book 1.0)
item.reason: every restart, deploy or watchdog kill killed every seat and charged an attempt per seat, and every process ran as the owner (F01, F11); two system units under their own users and one transient unit per seat replace it

item.what: one card when the store cannot open (book 1.0)
item.reason: a card is a commit to the store that cannot open (F15); the outside probe alerts instead

item.what: run.sh resolving the image digest and passing env into a container pane
item.reason: no container for the service; the digest pin survives for the pod images (N-22)

item.what: the Go service as a cluster pod (option C)
item.reason: C38 ruled test steps in pods and the service on the host; the store is a host file (SQLite does not work over a network filesystem)

the dead man's switch never fired in a 9.5 h outage

Health, Status, Reload, Drain, Retry kept
